To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genes TBP and PIIA are suitable reference genes for the normalization of gene expression in renal cell carcinoma.
TBP and PIIA are the two most suitable reference genes for the normalization of gene expression studies in clear cell renal carcinoma.
the genes PPIA, TBP, and RPLP0 are the most suitable reference genes for the normalization of gene expression studies of renal cell carcinomas by real-time PCR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reference gene panel that can be used to normalize RT-PCR results in human renal cell carcinoma.
a systematic evaluation of the most commonly used endogenous reference genes in clear renal cell carcinoma.
the development of a reference gene panel for future studies in renal cell carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PPIA and/or TBP are suitable reference genes for normalizing RT-PCR gene expression data from clear cell renal cancer.
the use of a single reference gene for normalization of target genes is not recommended.
the most suitable reference gene(s) for a specific experimental setting should be identified in each study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two most stably-expressed reference genes should be used for normalization.
TBP and PIIA are the best reference genes in renal cell carcinoma.
the use of a single reference gene should be avoided in gene expression studies of renal cell carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a combination of reference genes is preferable to the use of a single gene.
it is essential to validate the suitability of the housekeeping genes in the particular study design.

it is not sufficient to simply use a housekeeping gene without testing for its suitability in the respective experimental setup, as the expression stability of housekeeping genes is not always guaranteed.
